provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Surah Al-Asr
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite Surah Al-Asr correctly.
The pupils should be able to explain the meaning of Surah Al-Asr.
Introduction:
We have learned many short surahs. Today we will learn Surah Al-Asr which talks about time.
Content:
Surah Al-Asr means "The Time". It teaches us that all people are in loss. Except those who believe and do good deeds and teach others to be patient. Like when we help our parents at home or share our toys with friends.
Class activity:
Pupils will form groups and take turns reciting Surah Al-Asr with proper pronunciation.
Evaluation questions:
What is the meaning of Surah Al-Asr?
What does Allah say about time in this surah?
Name one good deed you can do today.
Summary:
Surah Al-Asr teaches us to use our time well for good deeds.

topics.title: Surah Al-Kawthar
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite Surah Al-Kawthar.
The pupils should be able to explain the importance of gratitude to Allah.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about time. Today we will learn Surah Al-Kawthar which teaches us to thank Allah.
Content:
Surah Al-Kawthar means "The Abundance". Allah gave Prophet Muhammad (SAW) many blessings. We should thank Allah for all good things like food, clothes and family. Like when our mother gives us food, we say "Alhamdulillah".
Class activity:
Pupils will write or draw three things they are grateful for today.
Evaluation questions:
What is the meaning of Surah Al-Kawthar?
Why should we thank Allah?
Name one blessing from Allah in your life.
Summary:
Surah Al-Kawthar teaches us to be grateful for Allah's blessings.

topics.title: Salat al-Jama'ah practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate how to lead prayer.
The pupils should be able to follow an imam properly.
Introduction:
We know how to pray alone. Today we will learn how to pray together in a group.
Content:
Salat al-Jama'ah is prayer in congregation. The imam stands in front. Everyone follows his movements. We must be quiet and listen. Like when our teacher leads us in morning assembly.
Class activity:
Pupils will take turns being imam and leading classmates in prayer.
Evaluation questions:
Who leads the prayer in congregation?
What should you do when the imam says "Allahu Akbar"?
Why is praying together important?
Summary:
In Salat al-Jama'ah, we follow the imam and pray together as one community.

topics.title: Hajj
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify Hajj as the fifth pillar of Islam.
The pupils should be able to explain the unity of pilgrims.
Introduction:
We have learned about prayer. Today we will learn about Hajj, another important pillar of Islam.
Content:
Hajj is the fifth pillar of Islam. It is a journey to Makkah for those who can afford it. Pilgrims wear simple white clothes. They all look equal before Allah. Like when we all wear our school uniform.
Class activity:
Pupils will draw pictures showing pilgrims in Ihram and performing Tawaf.
Evaluation questions:
What is the fifth pillar of Islam?
What do pilgrims wear during Hajj?
How does Hajj show unity among Muslims?
Summary:
Hajj teaches us unity and equality before Allah when we all serve Him together.

topics.title: Stories of the prophets
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the story of Prophet Adam.
The pupils should be able to list lessons from Prophet Nuh's life.
Introduction:
Muslims believe in many prophets. Today we will learn about some important prophets and what we can learn from them.
Content:
Prophet Adam was the first man created by Allah. Prophet Nuh built an ark to save believers from the flood. Prophet Ibrahim was ready to sacrifice his son for Allah. They all taught us to trust Allah and be good. Like when we trust our parents.
Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to act out a story of one prophet.
Evaluation questions:
Who was the first prophet?
What did Prophet Nuh build?
What lesson can we learn from Prophet Ibrahim?
Summary:
The prophets teach us important lessons about faith and obedience to Allah.

topics.title: The Prophet's family
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name Prophet Muhammad's wife Khadijah.
The pupils should be able to describe Fatimah's good qualities.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about prophets. Today we will learn about Prophet Muhammad's family members.
Content:
Khadijah was Prophet Muhammad's first wife. She was very kind and believed in him. Fatimah was his daughter. She was patient and helped the poor. We should learn their good manners. Like when we help our siblings.
Class activity:
Pupils will draw a picture of Prophet Muhammad's family and write one good quality about each.
Evaluation questions:
Who was Prophet Muhammad's first wife?
What good quality did Fatimah have?
How can you be like Khadijah or Fatimah?
Summary:
The Prophet's family showed us kindness, patience and helping others.

topics.title: Truthfulness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite a hadith about truthfulness.
The pupils should be able to give examples of honest choices.
Introduction:
We have learned about the Prophet's family. Today we will learn about truthfulness, which is very important in Islam.
Content:
The Prophet Muhammad (SAW) said "Truthfulness leads to righteousness and righteousness leads to Paradise". Being truthful means saying what is true. Like when you return money you found instead of keeping it.
Class activity:
Pupils will role-play situations where they choose to tell the truth.
Evaluation questions:
What did the Prophet say about truthfulness?
Give an example of being truthful at school.
Why is telling the truth important?
Summary:
Truthfulness leads to righteousness and Paradise, so we must always be honest.

topics.title: Charity
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain the importance of giving.
The pupils should be able to list different forms of sadaqah.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about truthfulness. Today we will learn about charity, which is giving to others.
Content:
Charity is giving to those in need. It can be money, food or help. Allah loves those who give. Like when we share our lunch with a friend who forgot theirs.
Class activity:
Pupils will make a list of things they can give as charity in their community.
Evaluation questions:
What is charity in Islam?
Name two forms of sadaqah.
How does Allah feel about those who give charity?
Summary:
Giving charity helps others and brings us reward from Allah.

topics.title: Peace and forgiveness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how to pardon others.
The pupils should be able to describe how to make peace.
Introduction:
We have learned about giving. Today we will learn about peace and forgiveness, which are important in Islam.
Content:
Islam teaches us to forgive others and make peace. The Prophet said "Forgive others so that Allah may forgive you". When someone hurts us, we should forgive them. Like when a friend accidentally breaks your toy.
Class activity:
Pupils will practice saying "I forgive you" to classmates in role-play situations.
Evaluation questions:
What does Islam teach us to do when someone hurts us?
Why should we forgive others?
How can you make peace with someone you argued with?
Summary:
Forgiving others and making peace pleases Allah and brings us peace of mind.

topics.title: Revision and recitation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite all surahs learned this term.
The pupils should be able to explain the main lessons from each surah.
Introduction:
This week we will review all we have learned this term about Islamic studies.
Content:
We will recite Surah Al-Asr, Surah Al-Kawthar and other surahs we learned. We will remember lessons about time, gratitude, prayer, Hajj, prophets, truthfulness and charity. Like reviewing our notes before an exam.
Class activity:
Pupils will have a praise concert where they recite the surahs beautifully.
Evaluation questions:
Which surah talks about time?
What is the fifth pillar of Islam?
Name one lesson from Prophet Ibrahim's story.
Summary:
We have reviewed all important lessons from this term and will continue to practice our recitation.
